To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of a DNA base lesion, 8 oxoguenine (OG), in a promoter region of a gene, leads to an increase in gene expression, and that this is due to a change in the DNA conformation, which allows for a different set of proteins to bind and regulate gene expression.
oxidative damage to DNA bases due in G quadruplex folding sequences of gene promoters is a novel epigenetic modification that leads to increased gene expression.
oxidative damage to guanine bases within a G quadruple forming sequence in gene promoter DNA is epigenetic, regulating gene transcription via BER.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oxidative DNA damage in the epigenome.
the impact of oxidative stress on the genome and the role that oxidative damage to guanine bases has in the epigenetic regulation of gene expression.
the role of oxidized DNA bases in gene regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of OG in PQS is an epigenetic event that leads to gene activation.
the formation of OG within a G quadruplease forming sequence in a gene promoter leads to gene activation via BER.
ROS mediated oxidation is a signaling agent to initiate BER in gene promoters, which can impact gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ROS mediated DNA damage is an epigenetic event that can be exploited to regulate gene transcription via BER.
the presence of OG in a G quadruple forming sequence in a gene promoter leads to a ~300% increase of gene expression.
oxidative stress can lead to epigenetic modifications in DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxidative damage to DNA is epigenetic.
oxidative damage to DNA bases is epigenetic.
the oxidative DNA damage lesion OG can be considered an epigenetic mark.
